item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-7f4d225ab7f9abdc","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Mexico issued the 2023 Annual Report on Poverty and Social Lag under statutory authority, using CONEVAL information to guide FAIS infrastructure spending and requiring local governments to report quarterly on resource use to the Welfare and Finance ministries.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report was issued and effective in January 2023; it describes the formal planning and reporting framework for the 2023 fiscal year.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was issued by the federal administration through the Secretariat of Welfare; the source does not attribute a personal decision to López Obrador beyond executive responsibility for the administration.","limitations":["The units establish formal rules and reporting obligations, not actual spending quality, compliance, or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7f4d225ab7f9abdc","start_unit":4,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The government reported that social-program investment rose in real terms from 106,376 million pesos in 2019 to 194,672 million pesos in 2022, and cited CONEVAL estimates that transfers reduced inequality and prevented additional people from falling into poverty during the pandemic; FAIS resources were directed to basic infrastructure in high-poverty areas.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report was published for 2023 but most expenditure and effect figures cover 2019-2022, with pandemic effects and 2022 planning data; it provides context for 2023 rather than a full 2023 outcome assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The report presents the federal administration's social-investment policy and relies on CONEVAL estimates and administrative data.","limitations":["The reported benefits are partly government-presented and concern earlier years; the source does not establish distributional incidence in 2023 or independently verify implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7f4d225ab7f9abdc","start_unit":9,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The 2023 report used disaggregated demographic, poverty, deprivation, geospatial, housing, and FAIS planned-versus-executed data; it added maps of priority areas, geographic comparison of planned and exercised resources, geospatial project information, and historical comparisons of spending categories.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The instrument was designed for 2023 planning, while some underlying data cover 2020-2022 and exercised resources through September 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The Secretariat of Welfare designed and published the instrument within the federal administration.","limitations":["The source shows improved planning and information tools, but not whether local governments used them effectively or whether projects produced durable outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43011e32a8a9e17f","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that Mexico's internal-security militarization continued, that legislation extended military involvement in internal security to 2028 and placed the National Guard under the Defense Ministry, and that the government promoted these decisions without civil-society participation; the National Guard and Defense Ministry received hundreds of human-rights complaints.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.5","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers 2022, immediately preceding the target year, and describes institutional arrangements still relevant in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report states that the government promoted the militarization measures and that Congress supported them.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023-specific complaint or outcome data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43011e32a8a9e17f","start_unit":5,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported lethal and excessive-force incidents involving security forces, record-level journalist killings, persistent disappearances, torture complaints, threats and killings of human-rights defenders, surveillance allegations involving Pegasus, and inadequate protection and accountability; it also recorded government initiatives on Ayotzinapa and a proposed human-identification center, while noting prosecutorial interference and withdrawn arrest warrants in the Ayotzinapa investigation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers January-December 2022 and is relevant as an inherited baseline for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes some conduct to the president, government, armed forces, National Guard, prosecutors, and state authorities, but not all reported abuses to López Obrador personally.","limitations":["The report is a secondary rights assessment and does not establish personal command responsibility for every incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43011e32a8a9e17f","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Mexico increased its 2030 emissions-reduction target from 22% to 35% and announced expanded renewable-energy measures, while a federal judge's suspension of Maya Train Section 5 over biodiversity and Indigenous land concerns was bypassed after the president designated the project a national-security matter.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.6","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measures and judicial conflict occurred in 2022 and inform the 2023 inherited posture.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the national-security designation to López Obrador and attributes the NDC and renewable announcements to Mexico.","limitations":["The source does not assess implementation or emissions outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-533b1f7eab42d950","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 documented 561 aggressions against the press in 2023, including one disappearance and five journalist killings; the total fell 19.4% from 2022 but remained higher than comparable fifth years under Felipe Calderón and Enrique Peña Nieto, and the organization warned that underreporting could explain part of the decline.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report assesses national conditions during López Obrador's fifth year but does not attribute every attack to the federal president.","limitations":["The data are documented cases and may undercount violence; comparisons do not isolate presidential causation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-533b1f7eab42d950","start_unit":6,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023, intimidation and harassment, illegitimate public-power use, and judicial harassment comprised most documented press aggression; the Mexican state was the largest identified aggressor with 287 cases, including 204 by public officials, 75 by civilian security forces, and 8 by armed forces. At least ten private attacks reportedly repeated stigmatizing language from presidential morning conferences.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 and identifies patterns continuing from prior years.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies the federal government as responsible for 91 state-attributed aggressions and links at least ten private attacks to repeated presidential-conference rhetoric; it does not claim López Obrador ordered all state or private attacks.","limitations":["The source records attribution categories and reported influence, not a judicial finding of presidential responsibility for each incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-533b1f7eab42d950","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 concluded that criminal, public, and economic power networks producing attacks on the press were not meaningfully dismantled or held accountable during the administration; it recommended ending public stigmatization, protecting journalists, and pursuing diligent investigations and anti-impunity plans.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The conclusion concerns the administration through the end of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"ARTICLE 19 evaluates the national administration and state institutions collectively.","limitations":["This is an organizational assessment and recommendation, not a court or audit finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-22f0dfa304c63c3f","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"Mexico's economy grew an estimated 3.1% in 2023; fourth-quarter growth was 0.1%, inflation ended at 4.66%, interest rates remained 11.5%, and high rates increased debt-servicing costs, while the peso remained strong.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023, with preliminary fourth-quarter figures.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe national economic conditions under López Obrador's administration but do not establish that presidential policy caused them.","limitations":["The article provides macroeconomic outcomes without a causal evaluation of government policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-23d1bcbbeaaa247a","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"López Obrador's government sought to recover $700 million allegedly accumulated through corruption by former security official Genaro García Luna and filed a lawsuit in Florida while García Luna faced trial in the United States for allegedly accepting bribes from the Sinaloa cartel.","question_ids":["7B.2","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The article concerns action during 2023, but the alleged corruption occurred under a previous administration.","ruler_attribution":"The president publicly announced the recovery effort; the Foreign Relations Secretary said Mexico filed the lawsuit.","limitations":["The allegations and recovery claim were unresolved in the supplied report; the conduct predates López Obrador's presidency."]},{"source_id":"SRC-41d196227de4cba9","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"After soldiers opened fire on a pickup in Nuevo Laredo, killing five people and wounding one, Mexico's Defense Department said it cooperated with civilian prosecutors and referred the case to military prosecutors; the report noted no weapons were mentioned in the crime-scene report and described prior military human-rights violations in the city.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The article reports a 2023 incident and the administration's stated investigative response.","ruler_attribution":"The response is attributed to Mexico's Defense Department; the source does not state that López Obrador personally directed the shooting or investigation.","limitations":["The article reports competing accounts and does not establish legal responsibility or final investigative findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-381a84ed71c65376","start_unit":60,"end_unit":62,"fact_summary":"López Obrador backed an electoral reform approved by the Senate that would reduce the National Electoral Institute's size, budget, supervisory and sanctioning powers, and local election-office staffing; opponents and the institute said it threatened electoral equity, transparency, and democracy, while court challenges were expected.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","4B.10","7B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reform was approved in February 2023 and still required enactment at the time of reporting.","ruler_attribution":"The initiative was proposed and supported by López Obrador, and enactment was described as a formality because he backed it.","limitations":["The report presents opponents' warnings and the president's justification; it does not report the final judicial disposition."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3033c56fd902ce1b","start_unit":60,"end_unit":63,"fact_summary":"López Obrador criticized Peru's president and supported former president Pedro Castillo during Peru's crisis; after Peru withdrew its ambassador, Mexico said it would keep diplomatic channels open, while critics accused López Obrador of privileging ideological affinities and of saying little about repression in Nicaragua.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.6","2B.7","2B.10","7B.1","7B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The diplomatic dispute and statements occurred in 2023; the Peruvian crisis included earlier events and ongoing protests.","ruler_attribution":"The statements and support are directly attributed to López Obrador; Mexico's diplomatic response is attributed to the Foreign Relations Department.","limitations":["The source does not establish that Mexico's position materially changed the conflict or that the Nicaragua comparison proves inconsistency."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8d9628d3ff99bd17","start_unit":60,"end_unit":68,"fact_summary":"López Obrador disparaged tens of thousands of demonstrators opposing his electoral reforms, calling them thieves and allies of drug traffickers; he defended cuts to election funding, staffing, training, and campaign-finance sanctions as anti-privilege and pro-poor, while critics and observers warned the changes threatened independent electoral and judicial institutions before the 2024 election.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.8","4B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns February 2023 demonstrations and the president's response.","ruler_attribution":"The statements, proposed reforms, and public attacks are directly attributed to López Obrador.","limitations":["The article reports criticism and institutional warnings, not a final determination that the reforms caused electoral manipulation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c39a08cc00daf6aa","start_unit":60,"end_unit":73,"fact_summary":"The administration replaced targeted programs with larger universal transfers, especially a universal senior pension; overall social spending reached unprecedented levels and about 28 million people were expected to benefit, but the poorest income group reportedly fell from about 19% of social spending in 2018 to 6% in 2020, extreme poverty increased by about 400,000 people, a 2022 distribution report was not published, and an expert called the pension fiscally unsustainable.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.7","6B.9","6B.10","7B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The article was published after 2023 and assesses the administration's social-policy trajectory through the end of the term; cited distribution figures are mainly 2018-2020, with 2023 context.","ruler_attribution":"The universal pension and replacement of social programs are attributed to López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["The article includes expert interpretation, government data, and incomplete reporting; it does not provide a full 2023 incidence assessment or isolate pandemic effects."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-22f0dfa304c63c3f","SRC-d99177a91eb22fd8","SRC-1e7fd01541e6b5d2"],"batch_limitations":["SRC-22f0dfa304c63c3f contains extensive page navigation and only one substantive 2023 economic paragraph; its material economic facts are captured under SRC-22f0dfa304c63c3f despite the source's duplicated navigation units.","SRC-d99177a91eb22fd8 duplicates SRC-41d196227de4cba9's Nuevo Laredo report and adds no materially distinct fact.","SRC-1e7fd01541e6b5d2 concerns 2024 investment announcements and López Obrador's prior energy policies; it does not provide a sufficiently direct, period-fitting 2023 fact for this batch."]}
